newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices weak, demand modest.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices weak, demand modest.

text.p: Subdued demand and lack of new leads continued to depress Thai rubber prices while the government failed to conclude a deal to buy a new lot of rubber, trade sources said on Friday.
Unless the government was willing to raise its bid for 5,000 tonnes of RSS3 grade it wanted to buy above 117 U.S. cents per kg, there would be no deal, they told Reuters.
The government has been inquiring since last Friday to buy a fresh quantity after purchasing 26,400 tonnes since March 5.
"The supplies of RSS3 were tight. The recent rain has affected the quality of rubber. Most producers can produce only RSS4 and RSS5," said one trader in southern Hat-Yai.
"Some shippers even had to delay their March/April shipments of RSS3 to Japan. The government will have to pay more than 117 if it really intends to buy," he said.
The offered price now was around 120 U.S. cents per kg.
Overall demand remained weak, reflecting the regional trend. China bought modest amounts after it entered the market, offering prices of around 115 U.S. cents a kg which many found too low.
"I heard China bought around 1,000 tonnes of SIR rubber from Indonesia. But there was not much going on here," said one Bangkok trader.
The Thai benchmark RSS3 rubber was indicated around 116 U.S. cents a kg FOB Bangkok on Friday from 117-118 on Wednesday.
